startup_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a founder negotiation on equity split and vesting for my startup. This is step n1 of the founder agreement process. The actual agreement between co-founders happens through conversation and remains a human step you cannot conduct on my behalf, but please prepare all the supporting materials so the negotiation is well-informed.

First, ask me for: (1) the names of all founders and their intended roles, (2) each founder's relevant contributions so far (cash invested, time committed, IP or prior work brought in, full-time vs part-time status), (3) any prior verbal agreements or expectations already discussed, and (4) my target vesting structure preference if I have one (e.g., standard 4-year vesting with a 1-year cliff is the common market default).

Using this information, produce: a one-page comparison of 2-3 plausible equity split scenarios with rationale for each (based on factors like time commitment, cash contribution, idea origination, and prior work); a plain-language summary of standard vesting terms (4-year vesting, 1-year cliff is typical) and what a cliff means in practice; a list of discussion questions founders should address before finalizing (e.g., what happens if a founder leaves early, unequal time commitment, future dilution from hires or investors); and a short glossary of key terms (vesting, cliff, cap table, dilution) so all founders share a common vocabulary.

Compile this into a single document I can bring to the founder conversation. Do not draft legal agreements or make the final split/vesting decision — that negotiation and agreement remains a human step between me and my co-founders. When the materials are ready, report back with the document and a short checklist of open questions I still need to resolve with my co-founders before we can move to drafting formal agreements.

startup_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me complete post-incorporation founder paperwork using {{vendor}}, a legal-ops platform for generating founder agreements and IP assignment documents. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my company's legal name, entity type, and state of incorporation, (2) each founder's full legal name, email, and title, (3) the agreed equity split (shares or percentage per founder), (4) vesting terms (schedule, cliff length, acceleration provisions, and vesting start date), and (5) whether we already have a {{vendor}} account or need one created.

Once you have these inputs, log into {{vendor}} (or start account setup) and use its guided questionnaire/intake forms to populate: the founder stock purchase agreements, the IP assignment agreement, and any related post-incorporation documents (bylaws, board consent, stock ledger setup) with the founder details, equity split, and vesting terms I provided. Flag any questionnaire prompts that indicate a choice needs attorney review — note these clearly in your report rather than guessing an answer.

Do not submit, sign, or send the documents for signature. Once all forms are filled and the draft agreements are generated in {{vendor}}, compile a summary showing: each document generated, the key terms entered (split, vesting, IP assignment scope), and any attorney-review flags raised by the questionnaire. Present this summary along with a direct link/path to the drafts in {{vendor}} and stop for human sign-off before anything is sent for execution.

startup_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me route our founder agreements (founder agreement, IP assignment, etc.) for e-signature using {{vendor}}, our chosen legal-ops platform. Because sending the envelope changes a binding legal record, I must explicitly approve before anything is actually sent — your job is to prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: (1) the finalized document files or template names for the founder agreement and IP assignment; (2) full legal names, emails, and signing order/roles for each founder/signer; (3) confirmation that {{vendor}} is the platform I want to use and that I have configured credentials for it.

Then, using {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard:
- Create a document set/envelope bundling the founder agreement and IP assignment documents for the founding team.
- Populate signer names, emails, and routing order exactly as I provided.
- If {{vendor}} requires prerequisite forms or data before documents can be submitted for signature, retrieve and fill those out (for Clerky specifically, this is the call to list required forms via 'GET /v1/document_sets/{id}/forms').
- Prepare a clear summary: which documents are bundled, who signs in what order, and any outstanding forms or missing fields.

Do NOT click send, submit, or trigger the actual signature routing — leave the envelope in draft/ready state and stop for human sign-off. Report back with: the document set ID or reference, a list of signers with roles/order, any missing/outstanding items, and confirmation that everything is staged and awaiting my explicit approval to send.

startup_002:n3b.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the founder agreement signing step for our startup (founder agreement with IP assignment and vesting terms). Do not sign, approve, consent to, or submit anything on my or any founder's behalf — actually executing the signature is a policy-gated action that only each founder can perform personally.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the finalized founder agreement document(s) (including IP assignment and vesting schedule), the full legal names and email addresses of each founder, and which e-signature service we plan to use (e.g., DocuSign, HelloSign, Adobe Sign, or a similar platform) along with confirmation that I have configured credentials for it.

Using that information, please prepare everything short of the actual signing: draft the signing request/envelope with the correct document(s) attached, pre-fill each founder's name, email, and signature/date fields in the correct locations, set the signing order if one is required, and write a short cover message to founders explaining what they're signing and why. Also prepare a checklist covering: confirming each founder's identity/email is correct, verifying the agreement version is final, noting the required signing deadline (if any tied to 83(b) timing), and a place to log the completed, signed document once returned.

Do not send the envelope, click send, or trigger any binding action — assemble the draft and checklist, then stop for human sign-off. Report back with a summary of what you prepared, any open questions or missing information, and the exact manual steps I or the founders need to take to review and execute the signatures ourselves, since this remains a human step.

startup_002:n4.prompt:
You are helping me record our just-signed founder equity splits on our cap table using {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform. 

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available:
- Login access confirmation (assume I have configured credentials for {{vendor}})
- The signed founder agreement details: each founder's name, email, number of shares or percentage ownership, share class (e.g., common stock), price per share/par value, and issuance date
- Vesting terms per founder: start date, cliff length, total vesting period, monthly/quarterly schedule, and any acceleration-on-exit terms agreed in the founder agreement
- Confirmation of total authorized shares/company valuation basis if not already set up in {{vendor}}

Once you have this information, please:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Create or update the cap table entries for each founder, entering their share class, quantity, and issuance date exactly as specified in the signed agreement.
3. Set up the custom vesting schedule for each founder in {{vendor}}, including cliff, vesting duration, and any acceleration terms, so vested vs. unvested shares are tracked automatically.
4. Generate the electronic share certificates within {{vendor}} for each founder, linked to their cap table entry, but do not sign or finalize them on my behalf — leave them ready for each founder's own signature.
5. Double-check that the total shares issued match the fully diluted totals agreed in the founder agreement, and flag any discrepancies.

This part of the process remains a human step: the actual signing of the electronic certificates by each founder must be done by them individually — you should not sign or submit on anyone's behalf.

When done, report back: confirmation that all founder entries and vesting schedules are correctly entered in {{vendor}}, screenshots or summaries of each cap table entry, and a note on any certificates still awaiting founder signatures.

startup_002:n4b.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT execute) the 83(b) election filings for our founders' restricted stock grants. This is a policy-gate step: only each individual founder can lawfully sign the perjury-attested IRS election, so you must stop before any signing, mailing, or submission happens.

First ask me for anything missing: company legal name and address, each founder's full name and mailing address, grant date, number of shares granted, purchase price paid (if any), fair market value per share at grant, and the vesting schedule. Do not ask me for or record Social Security Numbers — leave those fields blank in the draft for each founder to fill in personally.

Then: (1) draft a complete 83(b) election letter for each founder using the standard IRS-required format (taxpayer info with SSN left blank, description of property, date of transfer, restrictions, FMV, amount paid, statement under penalty of perjury), (2) draft the required cover letter and a certified-mail checklist for sending to the correct IRS service center within 30 days of grant, (3) draft the transmittal letter/copy for the company's records, and (4) produce a checklist covering: signing in ink, making copies, mailing via certified mail with return receipt within the 30-day deadline, and retaining proof of mailing.

Do not sign, date the signature line, mail, or submit anything on my or any founder's behalf — that remains for each founder individually. Present me the drafted letters, cover letters, and checklist, flag the exact 30-day deadline date for each grant, and then stop for human sign-off so each founder can personally sign and mail their own election.

startup_002:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare (but NOT file) IRS Section 83(b) elections for our founding team after our founder agreements and equity grants are signed. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing details needed to fill out the election: each founder's full legal name, address, and Social Security Number/TIN; the company's legal name, address, and EIN; the grant/purchase date of the restricted stock; the number of shares granted to each founder; the price paid (if any) per share and total; and the fair market value per share on the grant date (and how it was determined, e.g., par value or a valuation).
2. Download the official IRS Form 15620 from https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f15620.pdf for reference, and draft a filled-in version of the required election statement/letter for each founder using the details gathered, following the format IRS Form 15620 specifies.
3. Calculate and clearly flag the exact 30-calendar-day filing deadline from each founder's grant/purchase date, since missing it forfeits the tax election.
4. Prepare a checklist for each founder covering: making 3 copies (one to mail to the IRS, one to keep, one to attach to their personal tax return), mailing via USPS certified mail with return receipt requested to the correct IRS address for their state, and retaining the mailing receipt/tracking number as proof of timely filing.
5. Note that after mailing, verifying IRS receipt/confirmation is a separate follow-up step that should be tracked using the certified mail tracking number, since the IRS does not send confirmation automatically.

Important: each founder must personally review, sign under penalty of perjury, and mail their own election — you cannot sign or submit on anyone's behalf. Once drafts and the checklist with deadlines are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off.
